header: Boots on before eight, and a desk that is still yours at four
lead: Half the office is out on sites most of the week. The half that is in should not have to hunt for somewhere to sit when they get back.
bodytext:
Field days start at the Hollerau yard. The vans are loaded the evening before, the instruments are checked against the pillar in the car park, and whoever is driving decides the order of the jobs — not the office. If a site turns out to be under water, we come back and do drawing work; nobody is asked to stand in a flooded ditch to keep a schedule that was written on a Monday.

Everyone has one desk, one monitor arrangement and one chair, including the people who use them twice a week. We tried hot desking in 2019 and stopped after five months: people stopped leaving their field books out, and the field books were how the office knew what was going on.

Overtime is recorded, paid and, if you would rather, taken as time. The apprentices go to college on Fridays and are not asked to make the day up.
